stories.h: Clayface: DC's gory body-horror origin story lands
sum: DC Studios' Clayface, directed by James Watkins (Eden Lake), follows Matt Hagen, a Hollywood actor who is disfigured in an attack and turns to an experimental treatment that leaves him a shapeshifting, clay-like monster. Tom Rhys Harries leads, with Naomi Ackie as the woman who stands by him.

Screen Daily's Tim Grierson credits Watkins with real B-movie grit and finds Harries sympathetic, praising the film's adult tone and graphic violence. But he says the story turns generic and the ending predictable, with too little novelty to fill a feature. Early reaction elsewhere singles out Harries and the brutal effects work.
pts: Runtime 108 min, rated D17+ in Indonesia
Now showing in Indonesian cinemas; US/UK from 23 Oct

stories.h: Wildwood: Laika's darkest stop-motion epic wins raves
sum: Laika's new stop-motion fantasy follows Prue, a Portland girl whose baby brother is snatched by crows and carried into a hidden magical forest. She sets out to find him with her classmate Curtis. Peyton Elizabeth Lee and Jacob Tremblay voice the kids, with Carey Mulligan as the film's villain.

FOX19's critic calls the animation a leap forward for the studio, praising the detailed world-building, camera work and Mulligan's voice performance, and reads the story as a reflection on grief and handmade craft. The film is rated PG-13 and noticeably darker than typical family fare, so parents of young children should take note. Festival reviews have been broadly strong.
pts: Rated PG-13: dark for small kids
Voices: Peyton Elizabeth Lee, Carey Mulligan

stories.h: Klara and the Sun: critics pan Waititi's Ishiguro adaptation
sum: Taika Waititi's take on Kazuo Ishiguro's novel stars Jenna Ortega as Klara, an AI-powered Artificial Friend chosen by a wealthy, sickly teenager in a polluted future, with Amy Adams as the girl's mother. It opened in the US and UK on 23 October.

Reviews have been harsh: the film sits at 20% on Rotten Tomatoes, and The Guardian, The Times and The Telegraph all went low, mostly arguing Waititi's ironic, comic style clashes with the book's quiet melancholy. Screen Daily is the notable dissent, calling it an engaging, faithful fairytale with a strong Ortega performance, if overstuffed in its final act.
pts: In US/UK cinemas from 23 Oct; wider rollout to follow
Cast: Jenna Ortega, Amy Adams, Steve Buscemi

stories.h: Beautiful Pain: well-meant Indonesian drama falls short
sum: Dmaz Brodjonegoro's feature debut stars Raihaanun as Niken, a single mother who leaves an abusive marriage and starts an acting career, only to face harassment and slander that threaten her reputation and custody of her children. Baim Wong, Tarra Budiman and Jajang C Noer co-star; Hanung Bramantyo co-wrote.

CNN Indonesia's Endro Priherdityo praises its clear message about women's empowerment and committed turns from Raihaanun and Siti Fauziah. But he finds the conflicts too simple, the husband one-dimensional and the drama sometimes soap-like, with muddled flashbacks and small logic slips. Relatable, he concludes, rather than deeply affecting.

stories.h: Laut Bercerita closes Jakarta Film Week tonight
sum: Yosep Anggi Noen's adaptation of Leila S. Chudori's bestselling novel closes the sixth Jakarta Film Week on 25 October, the same evening the festival's competition winners are announced. Set in 1991 under the New Order, it follows student activist Biru Laut, played by Reza Rahadian, and the people left behind when activists disappear.

The film world-premiered in the main competition at Busan earlier this month. Dian Sastrowardoyo, Christine Hakim, Eva Celia and Yunita Siregar co-star, and Chudori co-wrote the script. Jakarta Film Week ran 21 to 25 October at venues including CGV Grand Indonesia and Taman Ismail Marzuki.

stories.h: 80.6 million cinema tickets sold in Indonesia so far in 2026
sum: Indonesia's Ministry of Culture says 80.6 million admissions were recorded through October, with local films taking 59.3% (about 47.8 million) and foreign titles 40.7%. At least 139 Indonesian films have screened this year, averaging roughly 344,000 viewers each.

No local hit has broken out the way Jumbo and Agak Laen 2 did in 2025: Danur: The Last Chapter leads at about 3.6 million, ahead of Ghost in The Cell and Jangan Buang Ibu. Among imports, the Avengers: Endgame re-release combined total tops 12 million, followed by Spider-Man: Brand New Day near 7 million. Horror still dominates the local top ten.
pts: Top local film: Danur: The Last Chapter (3.6M)
Avengers: Doomsday and Dune 3 still to come

stories.h: Netflix this week: Animals and Sacrifice top the chart
sum: Netflix added 24 films in the US this week, mostly library titles such as Gladiator and Gladiator II, The Ides of March and several Bollywood favourites including Gully Boy and English Vinglish. New originals include Paralyzed by Hope, a Judd Apatow documentary about comedian Maria Bamford, and a Theo Von stand-up special.

On the movie chart, Ben Affleck's kidnapping thriller Animals held the top spot for the week, followed by Sacrifice, Romain Gavras's cult thriller starring Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy. Regional catalogues differ, so check availability in Indonesia.
pts: New doc: Paralyzed by Hope (Maria Bamford)
US list; Indonesian catalogue may vary

stories.h: Tokyo film festival opens tomorrow with Garin Nugroho in competition
sum: The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival runs 26 October to 4 November, opening with Zeze Takahisa's music drama Sukiyaki and closing with Yeon Sang-ho's Korean zombie thriller Colony. Takashi Yamazaki's Godzilla Minus Zero is the centrepiece screening.

Fifteen films compete for the Tokyo Grand Prix, seven of them world premieres. Indonesia is represented by veteran director Garin Nugroho's Red Before Dawn, premiering in the main competition alongside Singapore's Magic Atlas by Sun Xun.
pts: Indonesia in competition: Red Before Dawn

stories.h: France unrest: cinemas close early as Hollywood shoots worry
sum: Protests over living costs and school conditions that began on 17 October have turned into riots in parts of France, and curfews in Paris, Marseille and Lyon are forcing cinemas to shut early. The national cinema federation says 20 to 30 venues are directly affected, with Paris's UGC Les Halles moving its last show to 7pm.

Several Hollywood productions are filming in the region, including The White Lotus season 4 on the Riviera and a Natalie Portman project in Nice. Shoots have not been halted, but studio security teams have warned crews to avoid Paris and Marseille, and French producers fear US projects may think twice.
pts: 20 to 30 French cinemas affected by curfews
Productions on alert, none halted yet

stories.h: Fontaines D.C. go dark New Wave on Dopamine Chamber
sum: The Dublin band's fifth album, out 16 October on XL, swaps guitar grit for a synth-heavy, dystopian New Wave palette that Consequence likens to Depeche Mode. Reviewer Paolo Ragusa says it keeps the band's habit of drawing listeners in before turning on them, and that it refuses to simplify even as their audience grows. A recurring theme of screens, film and spectatorship gives it a loose argument.

Highlights are the hypnotic lead single "Marianne", the quietly bitter "Happy for You" and the frantic "Tongue". The weak points: there is no obvious festival anthem, and the Rosalía duet "Where Is Gone?" is called the driest track. Overall it reads as a bolder, better-built follow-up to Romance.
pts: For fans of Depeche Mode, Romance-era Fontaines

stories.h: Stereogum's 5 best songs of the week
sum: Stereogum's weekly staff picks lean indie this time. Cloud Nothings' "Death Keeps Me Alive" gets the strongest praise, possibly the band's best song, adding metal heft to their old chaotic energy. Worldpeace DMT's "Ringtone" is a charming love song that revives 2000s blog-era twee with a cyborg twist.

The rest: sadie's buoyant "Little Things", which makes ordinary life feel magical; Hannah Frances' "Circadian Heart", a restless folk-jazz track about chasing emotionally unavailable people that ends cathartically; and Bassvictim's "White Flag", a combative lo-fi electroclash song about surrender.
pts: Start with Cloud Nothings, "Death Keeps Me Alive"
Five tracks, roughly 20 minutes of listening
For fans of noisy indie and art-folk

stories.h: Cloud Nothings go heavy on new album
sum: Cloud Nothings announced What Kind of Hell Did You Survive?, a nine-track album due 29 January on Pure Noise. It follows 2024's Final Summer. Frontman Dylan Baldi says the record pays tribute to heavy music he has been listening to, naming Queens of the Stone Age, Motörhead, Earth and Electric Wizard.

The lead single "Death Keeps Me Alive" is a doomy riff-driven track, with a video by Alex Scalzo-Brown. Stereogum compares it to Cave-In and the Wipers. The band also listed 12 November dates in the UK, Spain and Portugal.
pts: For fans of Attack On Memory, QOTSA

stories.h: Ugly's proggy debut The South Facade dazzles
sum: South London's Ugly, a live fixture for about a decade, released their debut The South Facade on 23 October. Best Fit's Cal Cashin says they have moved from early indie rock, influenced by King Krule and Bloc Party, into jazz fusion and prog, chasing the open spirit of 1970s music rather than showing off.

The review says the dense arrangements and bursts of fierce playing stay catchy because sweet melodies balance them. It points to Steely Dan, Primus and XTC as reference points and to Black Country, New Road as peers. It calls the album one of 2026's most creative debuts, with "Gavement" as its peak.
pts: For fans of Black Country, New Road

stories.h: Michael Kiwanuka's Fudge, made before his stroke
sum: Kiwanuka's new album Fudge (Polydor, out 23 October) was finished before the stroke that upended his life. NME's Fred Garratt-Stanley says it continues 2024's Small Changes, with warm guitars, soft soul and strings, but is more playful and experimental and has some darker corners.

Knowing about his illness and recovery gives the vocals and lyrics extra weight, and the review frames the record as a snapshot of an artist just before a turning point. Standouts named are "Sing", "California", "Drowning in Your Heart" and "Love In My Heart".
pts: For fans of Small Changes, Love & Hate

stories.h: Ryan Gosling's Dead Man's Bones return after 17 years
sum: Dead Man's Bones, the eerie indie project from Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields, posted a spooky teaser promising new music on 27 October, just before Halloween. ANTI-, which released their 2009 self-titled debut, shared the teaser too. The post doesn't say whether it's a single, EP or album, or give a title.

The 2009 record featured the Silverlake Conservatory Children's Choir, and the band toured briefly around that Halloween before going quiet. Fans had spotted hints from Gosling's stylist beforehand, and Eva Mendes reposted the teaser.
pts: For fans of haunted, choir-backed indie

stories.h: The Black Parade turns 20: why it's MCR's masterpiece
sum: Tom Breihan's anniversary essay argues My Chemical Romance's 2006 album is a true classic because the band went all-in on a huge theatrical concept. He says the costumes, the concept and producer Rob Cavallo placed them alongside the rock giants of the '70s to '90s rather than their emo peers. He admits he underrated the album at the time.

He ties it to the mid-2000s emo boom, the last time guitar rock ruled youth culture. He also recalls that it debuted at No. 2 behind the Hannah Montana soundtrack, went quadruple platinum and gave the band their only top-10 hit. He praises "I Don't Love You" as a rare modern power ballad and calls "Teenagers" his favourite.
pts: Start with "Welcome To The Black Parade", "Teenagers"
The reunited band plays it in full on tour
stories.q: My Chemical Romance The Black Parade

stories.h: Indie rock club Bottom of the Hill is saved
sum: San Francisco's Bottom of the Hill, a long-time stop on the indie rock touring circuit, won't close after all. Its owners announced in January that 2026 would be its last year, but after an outpouring of support they decided to sell instead. The buyer is Michele Bronson, a biotech scientist who has been a regular since the early '90s.

She plans to keep the staff, keep it independent and focused on emerging artists, keep taking no cut of band merch sales, and maybe bring back its old Sunday barbecues. After a month-long refit, the outgoing owners will host a farewell week of shows at year's end, including Shannon Shaw and Mark Eitzel.
pts: New owner keeps the staff and booking ethos
Closes for one month for a refit
Farewell week of shows at year's end

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: Telfar SS27: Paris invite, Brooklyn runway
sum: Telfar teased a Paris Fashion Week comeback for 6 October, then put the actual SS27 show on in Brooklyn and livestreamed it to the guests waiting in Paris. The collection turned office suiting inside out for the street and brought in pixelated leopard and snake prints, made by scanning real skins, on sheer shirts and baby tees.

New T-shirt shapes include a plus-sign 'Cross-T' and a 'Skew-T' inspired by pager culture. Inside-out fleece became cashmere-like cardigans, and worn sweats were padded into moto-style armour. A new mystery bag shape appeared on the runway and is due next year. A big sample sale opened alongside the show.
pts: Shown 6 Oct 2026, Brooklyn, livestreamed to Paris

stories.h: Salomon x Protect 'Slushie' drops Oct 28
sum: London streetwear label Protect has redone Salomon's ACS NEXT with a 'Lava Falls/Cyber Yellow' colourway. Gradients in the style of a slushie drink fade across the upper, with bright yellow hits and sharp accents throughout.

It's a global release this Wednesday, sold only through Protect's own webstore, so expect it to move fast. It's an easy way to add colour to a casual tomboy outfit, and the trail-runner shape keeps it practical for Jakarta rain.

stories.h: Converse x Vaquera turn a skate shoe into a kitten heel
sum: Vaquera, the New York label known for its oddball humour, has turned Converse's archived CS Pro-1 skate shoe into the VX-1 Heel, a kitten-heel version. It keeps the skate details: perforated suede, a padded mesh tongue, wide laces through moulded eyelet covers, the Star Chevron logo and a gum sole, with a see-through heel added.

Kim Petras fronts the campaign, posed inside a tiny dollhouse to play with scale. It follows the pair's 2025 Chuck Taylor collab, and it's a cheeky way to wear sneakers when you'd rather not wear heels.

stories.h: Vans 'Meet The Vans' holiday: sequins, fleece, plaid
sum: For the second season of its 'Meet The Vans' holiday campaign, Vans cast musicians and skaters including Nettspend, Samara Cyn, Devon Again and Geoff Rowley. The collection has two halves. Weatherised Half Cab and Sk8-Hi pairs get thermal insulation and grippy soles. Old Skool, Knu Skool, Authentic and Mule Platform styles get party textures: high-pile fleece, metallic sequins and winter plaids.
The standout is a Premium Old Skool 36 with silver sequins on the eyestay and laces over grey-and-white tweed. It's skate-punk with some sparkle, and works with baggy jeans.

stories.h: Jakarta Fashion Week 2027 opens tomorrow at PIM 3
sum: JFW 2027 runs from 26 October to 1 November 2026 at City Hall, Pondok Indah Mall 3, under the theme 'City of New Lights'. 111 designers will show, alongside the Fashion Force Awards, Fashionlink and Dewi Fashion Knights programmes.

The SEA WAVES exhibition, run with the Ministry of Tourism, adds installations on Southeast Asian weaving and traditional craft. Tickets are sold through ISMAYA+. Some shows are open to the public after registering, while others are invite-only, so check the schedule before you head down to PIM.

stories.h: Focus x New Balance 480 'unicorn' skate shoe
sum: Scottish skate shop Focus has made a New Balance Numeric 480 inspired by Scotland's national animal, the unicorn, with trippy unicorn graphics. Teal suede and white pebbled leather nod to the Scottish flag, and orange accents are a wink at Irn-Bru soda.
It's on sale now through Focus, in a special box edition, and through other skate shops. A colourful, slightly silly skate shoe like this is a good fit for a tomboy-casual wardrobe.

stories.h: JW Anderson previews the teal 'Run Rabbit' runner
sum: Jonathan Anderson has given a first look at the 'Run Rabbit', a new running-style sneaker for JW Anderson. It takes the proportions of a modern runner and adds the label's exaggerated styling, in saturated teal suede with ochre-yellow accents.

The details are playful: two-tone patterned flat laces paired with a round teal rope lace, and an orange charm like a die with a running rabbit on it. Price, release date and stockists are still to be confirmed.

stories.h: KEEN x Collina Strada: hiking shoes with flowers
sum: Collina Strada, Hillary Taymour's colourful and eco-minded label, has reworked two KEEN outdoor shoes. The Targhee EXP boot gets a side zip and a big handmade rosette. The Jasper Rocks sneaker gets a translucent climbing sole, plaid and floral details, and a removable fabric flower clipped through the laces.
Both have vegan satin-look uppers inspired by Victorian boots, with recycled linings. It's gorpcore with a romantic twist that still feels sporty.

stories.h: Eden Sherry's laced leather lands on Chappell Roan
sum: Chappell Roan joined Charli xcx on tour for a viral 'Boom Clap' duet, wearing a slashed black leather top with grommets, held together by laces, from London designer Eden Sherry. Stylist Hunter Clem commissioned it to match the rock-leaning feel of Charli's latest era.

Sherry graduated from London College of Fashion in 2024 and launched her label in 2025. She works in deadstock leather and builds clothes to survive nights out. FKA twigs has also worn her work on a Rolling Stone cover. She hopes to stage her first live presentation next summer.
pts: Deadstock leather, made for nights out

stories.h: Cabinet Couture: the Instagram tracking officials' luxury
sum: Dazed profiles Cabinet Couture, an anonymous Indonesian Instagram account that reposts public photos of political elites, identifies the luxury goods they're wearing and lists the prices. It started in September 2025 after the protests over lawmakers' allowances and now has more than 277,000 followers.

The original handle was geo-blocked in Indonesia by the communications ministry. The team says officials' declared wealth often can't explain what they're seen wearing. Followers now send in tips, and people who work in luxury retail help identify the pieces. It shows fashion being used for accountability at home.

stories.h: Israel locks down Hebron, 2,000+ forced from homes
sum: Netanyahu ordered a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank after two Palestinian gunmen attacked an Israeli reserve base on Friday, killing two soldiers before being killed. In Hebron, the mayor told Al Jazeera 2,200 people have been forced from their homes, while Defence Minister Israel Katz put it at about 2,000 and said they cannot return until Israel deals with Hamas in the city.

The Palestinian Prisoners' Society reported around 70 arrests in raids across at least 15 areas. The PA and Israeli rights group B'Tselem called it collective punishment, and UN chief Guterres voiced deep concern over closures and demolitions. Analysts say politicians are exploiting the attack ahead of Tuesday's Israeli election.
pts: Israeli elections Tuesday 27 Oct; all West Bank crossings to close that day
Palestinian workers barred from most areas Sunday to Monday
Activist Issa Amro says about 800,000 people in the Hebron area are under closure

stories.h: Gaza bakeries shut as flour stops arriving
sum: Ten of Gaza's 17 operating commercial bakeries have closed because no commercial flour has entered for about 10 days, according to the head of Gaza's bakery owners' association. Residents are queuing for hours for bread, and Gaza's social development ministry warned of an imminent humanitarian catastrophe and accused Israel of a policy of starvation.

Israel suspended commercial shipments on 14 October, citing a tax dispute with Hamas-run authorities, which Hamas and importers deny. At the same time, the WFP is cutting food aid to more than 500,000 people over lack of funding. Under the October 2025 ceasefire Israel agreed to at least 600 aid trucks a day; about 200 enter on average.
pts: 21 WFP-backed bakeries cover only about a quarter of bread needs
UN/IPC: 1.4 million people face crisis-level hunger or worse
More bakeries may close within days without new flour

stories.h: Activists win injunction, take US Gaza case to ICC
sum: A Seattle-based group, Taxpayers Alliance Against Genocide, together with DAWN, won a preliminary injunction on 13 October blocking the Trump administration from targeting them for working with sanctioned parties. They had argued that Executive Order 14203, which threatens fines up to $1 million and 20 years in prison for providing a service to sanctioned figures, violated their free-speech rights.

The order had stopped them sharing evidence with UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese and ICC officials. In a Mondoweiss op-ed, founder Tariq Ra'ouf says the group will now submit over a year of evidence to the ICC alleging top US officials aided genocide in Gaza, days after Washington sanctioned the entire court.
pts: US sanctioned the whole ICC on 9 October
Evidence includes testimony from ex-GHF contractor Anthony Aguilar
Palestine is a Rome Statute state party, giving the ICC jurisdiction

stories.h: AIPAC drops endorsements as its brand turns toxic
sum: Citing Jewish Insider, Mondoweiss reports that AIPAC will stop endorsing candidates and stop directly bundling donations to them, about five years after it launched its super PAC. Michael Arria argues the change reflects how unpopular the lobby has become, after Democratic primary voters organised against it in 2026 and its money became a liability for some candidates.

AIPAC will keep spending through its United Democracy Project super PAC, which Arria says makes its role less visible rather than smaller. The New York Times reported about $9 million in AIPAC-linked money for Republican Mike Rogers against Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Senate race.
pts: IMEU poll: most likely voters in six swing states back blocking arms sales to Israel
Possible 2028 Democrats like Newsom and Buttigieg still back Israel

stories.h: Prabowo's allies back away from free meals program
sum: Reuters, via The Jakarta Post, reports that two parties in Prabowo's ruling coalition have privately decided to distance themselves from his flagship free nutritious meals program, and a third fears electoral damage. The program has been hit by at least 57,000 food poisoning cases since January 2025 and by corruption arrests, including a former program chief in June.

An early-October SMRC poll found about 62% of the public opposed the program, and Prabowo's approval fell to 44.5%, his lowest yet. The coalition holds about 80% of the DPR, which has not cast a single dissenting vote on government bills. Gerindra insists the coalition remains solid.
pts: Rp 240 trillion budgeted for the program next year
One coalition member warns the bloc could fracture by mid-2027 without fixes

stories.h: Govt denies censoring wildfire criticism online
sum: As haze from forest and peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan spreads across the region, users of Instagram, Threads and TikTok say posts criticising the government's slow response were hidden or removed. Some allege feeds were tuned to suppress critical content.

Communications and Digital Minister Meutya Hafid denied the government removed posts, asked platforms to do so, or moderated algorithms, saying it is open to factual information about the fires. The article gives no figures on takedowns and names no affected accounts. The row follows student protests on 20 October demanding the fires be declared a national disaster.
pts: Minister says she has pressed platforms for algorithm transparency
No investigation or platform action announced
Comes amid wider concern over shrinking civic space

stories.h: Students rally as Prabowo marks two years
sum: Students and civil society groups protested in Jakarta, Bandung and Yogyakarta on 20 October, the second anniversary of Prabowo Subianto's presidency. In Jakarta, hundreds of students rallied at the Tugu Tani monument, while Greenpeace activists climbed the Welcome Monument at Bundaran HI to hang banners over the government's handling of the wildfires.

Demands included declaring the forest fires a national disaster, prosecuting companies responsible for environmental damage, protecting freedom of expression, tackling corruption, and making education and health care affordable. Fires across Sumatra, Kalimantan and Papua in a severe El Nino dry season have closed schools and disrupted flights.
pts: Protesters also raised cost of living and civil liberties
Haze has reached Singapore and Malaysia
Fires burning across Sumatra, Kalimantan and Papua

stories.h: HSBC to review halal fund's Palantir stake
sum: HSBC will review the Palantir holding in its Islamic Global Equity Index Fund, described as the UK's largest halal fund, after scrutiny from Muslim savers. Muslim outlet The Hyphen revealed the fund bought $38 million of Palantir shares in the first half of 2026. Palantir's CEO has publicly defended the Israeli military's use of its technology.

Nest, the UK state-backed workplace pension whose sharia fund invests in HSBC's fund for about 40,000 members, raised concerns after member inquiries. MEE's own analysis found the fund bought over $100 million in five Israeli-military-linked companies, including $35.7 million in RTX. HSBC says it will review the holding with independent advisers.
pts: No timeline or commitment yet to sell
Nest executives are in talks with HSBC
Pressure came from Muslim media and pension members

stories.h: Brazil's runoff today is a vote on Israel ties
sum: Brazilians vote today, 25 October, in a presidential runoff between incumbent Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro, who narrowly led the first round on 5 October. Mondoweiss argues the race is also a referendum on Brazil's stance toward Israel. Bolsonaro, a self-described evangelical, has pledged to move the embassy to Jerusalem, voiced support for settlers, and plans to join the Israel-led Isaac Accords.

Lula recalled Brazil's ambassador to Israel in 2024, joined South Africa's ICJ genocide case in 2025, and suspended arms exports to Israel, though he has not imposed a full embargo and trade continues. The piece frames Brazil as the last big holdout against a pro-Israel right turn in Latin America.
pts: Brazil is about a third of Latin America's population and economy
Evangelicals make up about 27% of the electorate
